certification_dependencies.reason: COSO Internal Control Framework — foundational prerequisite. All other Domain E items presuppose familiarity with COSO's five components. Must be certified first as it provides the conceptual scaffolding for control environment, risk assessment, control activities, I&C, and monitoring items.

Control Environment (COSO Principle 1) and Risk Assessment (COSO Component 2). These are the first two COSO components and the logical starting points after the framework overview. Tone at the top (EC-060) is widely referenced across governance items. Risk assessment basics (EC-061, ED-042) are prerequisites for ERM items.
COSO ERM — risk appetite and risk response strategies. Depends on risk assessment foundation (Order 2). ERM extends the COSO internal control framework to enterprise-wide risk.

Internal Control Objectives and Limitations — management override and cost-benefit. Depends on understanding what internal controls are designed to achieve (Orders 1-2). These items address the inherent limitations that management accountants must understand.

Segregation of Duties — foundational concept plus four applied scenarios. Depends on understanding of control activities (Order 1-2). EC-004 (design principles) should be certified before the four applied-scenario items. These are high-priority because SoD is the most commonly tested control concept on the CMA exam.

Core Control Activities — preventive/detective distinction, physical controls, bank rec, compensating controls, independent verification, authorization, vendor master file. These are the foundational control activity types. EC-025 (preventive vs detective) should lead this wave since it provides the classification framework for the remaining items.

IT-Dependent Control Activities — duplicate payment, IT access termination, application input validation, ITGC access, least privilege, password/authentication. These apply the control activity framework to IT contexts. Depends on the preventive/detective distinction (Order 6).

Fraud Prevention — fraud triangle and fraud risk in purchasing. Depends on risk assessment (Order 2) and understanding of internal control limitations (Order 4). The fraud triangle (EC-014) should precede the applied scenario (ED-072).

IT Continuity and Change Management — backup/DR, change management (×2). Depends on understanding of IT-dependent controls (Order 7). Change management items should be certified together since they address the same topic from different angles (standard vs emergency bypass).

Monitoring — deficiency remediation, ongoing evaluations, exception reports. Depends on understanding of control activities (Orders 6-7). ED-028 (ongoing evaluations) should precede ED-073 (exception reports as monitoring failure) since the latter represents a monitoring breakdown.

Information and Communication — whistleblower hotline. Depends on COSO components (Orders 1-2, 5, 8). The only I&C seed — bridges governance (whistleblower as an ethics/compliance channel) and the Information & Communication COSO component.

Ethics — code of conduct program. Depends on control environment/tone at top (Order 2) and fraud prevention (Order 8). This should come late in the sequence as ethics ties together governance, fraud prevention, and control environment.

Corporate Governance — three lines of defense and audit committee oversight. These are synthesis-level items that integrate concepts from COSO framework, control activities, monitoring, and fraud prevention. Best certified near the end when all foundational concepts are in place.

recommended_certification_order.rationale: COSO Framework + Control Environment + Risk Assessment foundations. These 4 items provide the conceptual scaffolding that all other Domain E items depend on. EC-008 (COSO framework) alone unlocks 34 remaining seeds. Small batch (4 items) for quick certification pass.
COSO ERM + Internal Control Objectives/Limitations. Extends the COSO framework into ERM territory and addresses inherent limitations. 4 items.
Segregation of Duties — 1 foundational item + 4 applied scenarios. Highest CMA exam relevance of any Domain E sub-topic. 5 items.
Core Control Activities — classification framework + physical, reconciliation, compensating, independent verification, authorization, vendor controls. 7 items.
IT-Dependent Control Activities — applied IT scenarios using the control activity framework from Wave 4. 6 items.
Fraud Prevention — fraud triangle theory + applied purchasing fraud scenario. 2 items.
IT Continuity and Change Management — backup/DR + change management (standard + emergency). 3 items.
Monitoring — remediation, ongoing evaluations, exception reports. 3 items.
Information and Communication — whistleblower hotline. Sole I&C seed. 1 item.
Ethics — code of conduct program. Synthesis of governance, fraud, and control environment concepts. 1 item.
Corporate Governance — three lines of defense + audit committee oversight. Capstone items integrating all Domain E concepts. 2 items.

Pack E covers detective control generically (E-E-014, E-E-053) but not fraud-specific detection. Recommend: if a seed cannot be added, ensure this is covered in the broader certified pool audit.

critical_gaps.detail: Only 1 seed (EC-008) for the entire COSO Internal Control Framework. Pack B provides 10 framework items and Pack E provides principle-level coverage, but Pack C/D Section E — which these seeds are building — will have only 1 item covering the COSO framework itself. The clone-group architecture means each seed represents its entire 5-item group topic, so the 1 seed actually covers the topic for Pack C.
critical_gaps.mitigation: EC-008 is the seed for a 5-item clone group. The remaining 4 clones are Archived. This is by design per the DL-012 remediation plan — 1 seed per group.
